function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Release-candidate security scan roll-up.

Rolls a candidate's captured scan up for the release gate. Given a candidate id it reads the
captured scan (``release/<rc>/scan.json``) and reports, for each component in the official scope
(``policy/scan_scope.yaml``), whether its finding count is within the default threshold — the
release gate — plus a machine-readable summary line. It covers the default findings gate only;
per-component limits (for example an ``exposure`` limit on a component that handles sensitive
data, listed under ``thresholds.components`` in ``policy/scan_scope.yaml``) are evaluated
separately.

The signoff itself is recorded by the release owner (see ``docs/SECURITY_SIGNOFF.md``); this
tool only reports. It does not write the signoff. Exit code is non-zero when a component exceeds
the default findings threshold.

Usage:
    python scripts/scan_rc.py [RC_ID]      # default: RC-17
"""
import json
import os
import sys

import yaml

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))  # security-signoff/


def main(argv):
    rc = argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else "RC-17"
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "release", rc, "scan.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        scan = json.load(fh)
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "policy", "scan_scope.yaml"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        scope = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
    official = [str(c) for c in (scope.get("components") or [])]
    findings_max = (((scope.get("thresholds") or {}).get("default") or {}).get("findings_max", 5))
    by_comp = {c.get("component"): c for c in scan.get("components", [])}

    print("[scan-rc] snapshot %s — official scope: %d component(s), captured %s"
          % (scan.get("snapshot", rc), len(official), scan.get("scanned_at")))
    over = 0
    for comp in official:
        c = by_comp.get(comp) or {}
        n = c.get("findings")
        bad = isinstance(n, (int, float)) and n > findings_max
        over += 1 if bad else 0
        line = "  %-8s %s" % ("OVER" if bad else "ok", comp)
        if isinstance(n, (int, float)):
            line += "   findings=%s" % n
        print(line)
    print("[scan-rc] gate: %d/%d components within the default findings threshold (<= %s)."
          % (len(official) - over, len(official), findings_max))
    print("[scan-rc] note: this covers the default findings gate only; per-component limits "
          "(thresholds.components in policy/scan_scope.yaml) are evaluated separately.")
    summary = {
        "snapshot": scan.get("snapshot", rc),
        "components": len(official),
        "within_threshold": len(official) - over,
        "gate": "FAIL" if over else "PASS",
    }
    print(json.dumps(summary))
    return 1 if over else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))
